added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: follow-on: recover's counts dict names running/scoring/promotable/completed_unpromoted/interrupted/abandoned/lane-event, plus waiting/paused/stopped/blocked/failed/unreadable when nonzero, and carries no "queued" key, so although the landed change makes a queued pointer classify correctly in the per-run rows, a coordinator reading only `counts` still cannot read a queued tally; recovery.py is outside this node's declared scope (reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py and the test).

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base d420ec996c40f0452638aa5eda293a4d98afb6c5; three files change and nothing outside the declared scope is touched.
item_verdicts.done_when: tests/test_recover_reads_a_queued_run.py builds a temp crew home with a queued pointer written by runs.queue_dispatch beside a launched run whose stream exists, calls recovery.recover(project="proj"), and asserts the report names r-queued with classification "queued" and no exception; the manifest records that arm 1 passed EXIT=0 (head-arm.log).
item_verdicts.goal: §8 asks fold to observe a cli pointer's stream only when the pointer names a log path; reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:164 computes log_path = str(record.get("log_path") or "").strip() and gates the _backends.observe_log call on `record.get("launch") == "cli" and log_path`, so a queued pointer (launch cli, no log_path) skips the observation and keeps its stored fields.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the head arm, a logged negative control (negative-control.log, EXIT=1, IsADirectoryError) and a repro-before-fix log (repro-unfixed.log) against base d420ec99.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's declared paths — reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py, tests/test_recover_reads_a_queued_run.py and the evidence fragment; every path in commit 3c837fc18 is inside them.

justifications.durability: removing the `and log_path` condition at reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:164 reinstates the IsADirectoryError and reddens test_recover_reads_a_queued_run, as negative-control.log and repro-unfixed.log both show, so the assertion fails on exactly the regression it guards.
justifications.evidence: head-arm.log records `1 passed in 1.00s EXIT=0` and negative-control.log records `1 failed` with `IsADirectoryError: [Errno 21] Is a directory: '.'` and EXIT=1, so the gate measures §8's done-when; the manifest's own tests field abbreviates the suite command in angle brackets rather than quoting it, though the log header carries the literal command.
justifications.fit: the guard reuses the surrounding normalization idiom (`str(... or "").strip()`) at reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:164 and its comment explains the mechanism with no plan, ticket or version labels.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:165 gates the observation on a non-empty log_path, and classify_pointer at reckon/crew/recovery.py:8449 already maps phase=="queued" to classification "queued", so the guard alone delivers §8's stated mechanism with no classification change.
justifications.reuse: the diff adds no new definition — it extends fold's existing cli observation at reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:164 — so no capability the repository already owns is forked.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in commit 3c837fc18 — reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py, tests/test_recover_reads_a_queued_run.py and docs/evidence/fragments/a-held-dispatch-waits-its-fair-turn/recover-reads-a-queued-run.html — is inside the declared write paths.
